title: Simulating Black Hole Thermality and Interior Scrambling on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Ryan Smith, Ewan Forbes, Iason Sofos Andrew Hallam, Jiannis Pachos
abstract: We implement a chiral spin-chain black hole simulator on IBM superconducting quantum hardware and probe, within a common microscopic framework, both semiclassical horizon physics and interacting quantum scrambling. We first measure the dispersion relation across the exterior, horizon and over-tilted interior regimes, reproducing the predicted evolution of the effective light-cone structure. To probe Hawking thermality, we prepare a localised excitation inside the horizon and monitor its density response at an exterior site, observing the predicted inverse relation between the peak arrival time and the surface gravity, thereby establishing a calibrated dynamical estimator of the Hawking temperature. Beyond the semiclassical regime, we continuously tune the interactions and distinguish non-exponential operator spreading in the free-fermion limit from Lyapunov-like OTOC decay in the strongly interacting chiral regime. These measurements use observable-specific Floquet circuits derived from the same parent chiral model, including its mean-field and coordinate-equivalent XY descriptions, to reduce circuit depth while preserving the physics relevant to each probe. Our results provide a unified programmable platform for studying horizon geometry, Hawking thermality and interacting scrambling on quantum hardware.
summary: This work implements a black hole analogue simulator on superconducting quantum hardware to probe fundamental physics. By tailoring quantum circuits, the authors measure key signatures of black hole physics, including the effective light-cone structure, the characteristic signal of Hawking temperature, and the transition from free-fermion to strongly interacting quantum scrambling. This establishes a unified, programmable platform for quantum gravity research.
main_problem: The paper aims to study both semiclassical black hole horizon physics (Hawking thermality) and strongly interacting quantum scrambling using a unified, programmable quantum simulation platform.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated the measurement of Hawking thermality and the distinction between free-fermion and strongly interacting scrambling dynamics on superconducting quantum hardware.
method: The study employs a chiral spin-chain black hole analogue Hamiltonian, which is decomposed into multiple, observable-specific Floquet circuits tailored for different physical probes.
model_or_system: The system is a chiral spin-chain black hole analogue simulated on IBM superconducting quantum hardware. The model includes three related lattice realizations: the full interacting chiral model, a mean-field (semiclassical) limit, and a free-fermion XY model.
key_observables: Dispersion relation (across exterior, horizon, interior), density response for Hawking thermality, and Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs) for scrambling.
important_parameters: Surface gravity, coupling profile gradient ($\alpha$), and the tunable interaction parameter ($\phi$) controlling the transition between free-fermion and interacting regimes.
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve using reduced, observable-specific circuits to manage circuit depth, and employing error mitigation techniques like Pauli twirling and Zero Noise Extrapolations (ZNE) for hardware measurements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the relationship between the three lattice Hamiltonians and their corresponding circuits, show measured dispersion relations across different spacetime regimes, and compare OTOC decay rates between different theoretical limits.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model (chiral spin-chain), derives multiple circuit approximations ($U_{MF}, U_{XY}, U_{int}$), and then systematically measures three distinct phenomena—geometry, thermality, and scrambling—using these tailored circuits on quantum hardware.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, hardware-implementable framework to test deep theoretical concepts from quantum gravity (like Hawking radiation and spacetime structure) using modern quantum computing tools.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Overview of the black hole quantum simulator and its hardware validation. (a) Relations among the lattice Hamiltonians, quantum circuits and effective theories considered in this work. The interacting chiral model HC reduces under mean-field theory to HMF, whose semiclassical geometry is coordinate-equivalent to that of the free-fermion XY model HXY. The circuits UMF and UXY reproduce their respective Hamiltonian dynamics in the small-time-step limit. The reduced circuit Uint instead isolates the non-free-fermionic sector of the parent chiral circuit used to probe scrambling.
